name: Peter J. Book
role: Mandan mason who opened Medora's brickyard and built its brick buildings
bio: Peter J. Book was a Mandan mason and contractor, known for building the People's block there, who tested Medora's butte clay in April 1884 and moved his family and five brick-makers to a yard south of town that month. He opened his first kiln in late May, was making pressed brick by June, and in August 1884 the Marquis gave him the contract for two brick cottages and asked him to plan a brick church. Over the winter he drew the brick plans for George Fitzgerald's new hotel and took the whole contract, and in March 1885 he also won the contract for an 85-foot slaughter-house smoke stack; the hotel was finished in May 1885. He was also a regular in the Bad Lands Gun Club shoots, and the paper mentioned "Pete Book's coal mine" up the river. In June 1885 he patented a lignite-burning brick kiln, and that summer he and most of his brick men worked on new buildings in Miles City, returning to Medora in September when the work there was done.
